name: Tai Shu-lun
bio: Tai Shu-lun is dated by Giles to the 9th century AD. His poem here is a New Year’s Eve alone at an inn.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: New Year's Eve at an Inn
poems.author: Tai Shu-lun
poems.text:
Here in this inn no friend is nigh;
We sit alone, my lamp and I,

A thousand miles from love and smiles,
To see another year pass by.

Ah me, that ever I was born!
Is life worth living, thus forlorn?

Youth, beauty, pass; and yet alas
It will be spring tomorrow morn.

poems.title: Chancing on Old Friends in a Village Inn
poems.author: Tai Shu-lun
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
While the autumn moon is pouring full
On a thousand night-levels among towns and villages,
There meet by chance, south of the river,
Dreaming doubters of a dream . . .
In the trees a wind has startled the birds,
And insects cower from cold in the grass;
But wayfarers at least have wine
And nothing to fear — till the morning bell.

poems.title: 過三閭廟 (Guo san lu miao)
poems.author: Tai Shu-lun
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
沅湘流不盡，屈子怨何深！
日暮秋風起，蕭蕭楓樹林。

poems.title: 客夜與故人偶集 (Ke ye yu gu ren ou ji)
poems.author: Tai Shu-lun
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 五言律詩. Also titled 江鄉故人偶集客舍.
poems.text:
天秋月又滿，城闕夜千重。
還作江南會，翻疑夢裏逢。
風枝驚暗鵲，露草覆寒蛩。
羈旅長堪醉，相留畏曉鍾。
